header.name: Wearable Applications, Research, Devices, Interactions (WARDI)
header.description: This is a course about the current paradigm of Wearable Computing. In this course, we will cover the origins, pioneering contributions, and principles of Wearable Computing. With this foundation, we will initiate our exploration into the space by learning how to design physical (device form factor), digital (applications) as well as human (interaction techniques) aspects of Wearables. You will develop the skills needed to conduct design of these three interrelated elements and also get a chance to apply them on short assignments and student-selected group projects. We will also discuss and critique both seminal and cutting-edge research in the domain to help you identify opportunities for new research that may begin with your class projects.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Identify the motivation, guiding principles, and challenges of Wearable Computing.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Develop skills pertaining to the design of a holistic interactive wearable system comprising of the physical, digital, and the human aspects.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Critique research published on novel applications, design of form factor, and sensor-based interactions of wearable computers.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Generate new project ideas that illustrate effective use of wearables for a problem you identify.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Plan and produce proof-of- concepts to test hypotheses about a wearable solution.
